input:
Integral of [e^(tan^-1 x)/(1+x^2)] * [(sec^-1(sqrt(1+x^2)))^2 + cos^-1((1-x^2)/(1+x^2))] dx, x>0 is

Options:
A. (tan^-1 x)^2 e^(tan^-1 x) + c
B. (tan^-1 x)e^(tan^-1 x) + c
C. (tan^-1 x)e^(2tan^-1 x) + c
D. (tan^-1 x)^2 e^(2tan^-1 x) + c

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Evaluate the integral containing e^(tan^-1 x)/(1+x^2) multiplied by inverse-trigonometric expressions.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Use substitution t = tan^-1 x; then sec^-1(sqrt(1+x^2)) becomes t and cos^-1((1-x^2)/(1+x^2)) becomes 2t.

key_formulas.identity_1: sec(t) = sqrt(1+tan^2 t) => sec^-1(sqrt(1+x^2)) = t for x>0

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Substitute t = tan^-1 x, simplify bracket to t^2 + 2t, integrate e^t(t^2+2t) dt.

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: Differentiating (tan^-1 x)^2 e^(tan^-1 x) reproduces e^(tan^-1 x)/(1+x^2)*(t^2+2t), matching the transformed integrand.
